newsitem.title: UK: Copper creeps higher in languid LME pre-market.
newsitem.headline: Copper creeps higher in languid LME pre-market.

text.p: Copper and aluminium were marginally firmer on Thursday morning in slow activity as the market wondered whether recent lows would hold.
Three months copper crawled up to $2,268 per tonne, up $12 from Wednesday's afternoon kerb close, but the volume of business was very light, traders said.
"There has been some nervous buying going one. The specs are looking for a bottom to buy," a senior trader said, referring generally to the metals complex.
Players are trying to second-guess the funds' next move -- whether they will try to extend the downside a bit more, he added.
Copper and aluminium appeared caught in a range, having put down lower boundaries during Monday's sell-off and then failed on subsequent upside moves.
Many metals were being pulled in opposite directions, caught between a damaged technical picture and fairly strong short-term fundamental situation as LME stocks show steady drawdowns.
Copper stocks were down by only 850 tonnes on Thursday, but the cumulative erosion has been an impressive 20,650 tonnes since April 7, when the LME launched daily reports.
Aluminium inventories fell by 3,075 tonnes on Thursday, bring the total drawdowns to 15,500 tonnes since April 7.
The market seemed to ignore the aluminium stock data, however, hovering at slightly firmer levels. Prices were up $5 to $1,552.
Technical analysts thought there was more scope on the downside for aluminium to test the year's low at $1,534, with the upside capped at Monday's high of $1,666.
Some light buying was also seen in nickel, which rose $15 to $7,270.

"Although the technical pattern remains weak, consolidation in a $7,110-$7,450 range is more likely as the right shoulder of a large head and shoulders pattern develops," broker Brandeis said in a commentary.
Most of the others were barely changed.
Zinc was unchanged at $1,241, but analysts believed Wednesday's weak close might indicate a test of $1,230 support was on the cards.
Lead was indicated slightly weaker at $635/37 after $639 on Wednesday and tin was also softer at $5,660, down $30.
Alloy was indicated at $1,445/53, little changed from $1,450.
